stepNotes.1: The facade exports auth, device-flow, Octokit, and repo helpers, while routes.js registers auth, PR, fork, branch, issue, and context HTTP endpoints and pr-status.js owns multi-remote discovery.
stepNotes.2: Production /api middleware requires the UI session and rate-limits calls; account projections omit tokens, but the temporary auth file is populated before chmod 0600, leaving a local exposure interval.
stepNotes.3: Discovery can return an upstream PR, yet update, merge, and ready resolve origin again and accept only a PR number; fallback search also filters same-name repositories without checking owner.
stepNotes.4: PR status caching is bounded but keyed only by directory, branch, and remote and is read before auth, so activation or disconnect can reuse another account's connected result; check details can fan out heavily.
stepNotes.5: Auth, OAuth transport, Octokit creation, repo parsing, and route orchestration have clear homes, but mutation schemas drop the resolved repository identity and check aggregation is duplicated in two handlers.
stepNotes.6: Most expected 403/404 gaps are narrowed and unknown errors rethrow, while default-branch lookup and per-repo list helpers suppress broader failures that can turn revoked auth into empty connected data.
stepNotes.7: The six passing tests cover four auth filesystem cases and two activation validation cases, leaving device flow, fork resolution, caches, fallback matching, and every PR operation without focused coverage.
stepNotes.8: The primary pass records one High fork-mutation defect, three Medium issues involving temp permissions, cache identity, and fallback ownership, plus Low amplification/error-reporting advisories; no Critical evidence exists.
stepNotes.9: Focused Vitest passed 2 files and 6 tests, and production registration plus the web API and UI call sites were checked to confirm the route-level conclusions beyond the isolated test app.
